model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the negative log probability of Mistralv0.2-Base when fine-tuned on six medical specialties—Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, and Pediatrics—evaluated on per-specialty terms. The vertical axis represents “Negative log probability,” ranging from -22 to -27, with lower values indicating better model performance (higher likelihood). The horizontal axis lists the six specialties, each associated with a group of six bars corresponding to the model’s performance on terms from each specialty. The legend indicates that each bar color corresponds to a specialty: light beige for Cardio, light orange for Gastro, medium orange for Infect, dark orange for Neuro, dark brown for Obstetrics, and black for Pediatrics. In each group, the first bar (light blue) represents the performance of the base Mistralv0.2 model without fine-tuning. Across all specialties, the base model consistently performs worse (higher negative log probability) than the fine-tuned versions. Fine-tuning generally improves performance, with the largest improvements seen in the Neuro and Pediatrics specialties. Within each specialty group, the bar corresponding to that specialty’s terms tends to be among the lowest (best performance), suggesting specialization enhances relevance. The bars are not sorted by height within groups, and no bars are visually emphasized beyond color coding. The chart visually conveys that fine-tuning improves model calibration on domain-specific terminology, with varying degrees of improvement across specialties.
